# Power Laws & Fat Tails: core idea behind Fatail

**Source:** [Just 4% of Stocks Created ALL the Market's Wealth | Power Laws & Fat Tails](https://youtube.com/shorts/BcA8gDbOjkE), Thousand Bagger (@thousandbagger), "One Model at a Time" Ep. 20/100, published 17 Nov 2026, 2:40.
**Transcript:** YouTube auto-generated English captions, lightly cleaned (the caption's "Excel" is the VC firm Accel, as the video description spells it).
**Saved:** 17 Nov 2026 for Vipul Anand's capital-growth research (Fatail).

## Why this matters for us

Fatail's job is to find mutual funds that can produce fat-tail (outsized-upside) returns. This video lays out that core idea:

- Returns follow a power law, not a bell curve. A few extreme winners create most of the wealth.
- Bessembinder (1926–2016, about 26,000 US stocks) found that about 4% of stocks created all the net gains over T-bills. Most stocks did worse than T-bills.
- The two rules for any investor:
  1. Don't sell a rare big winner too early.
  2. Never take a loss that could knock you out of the game.
- Fat tails cut both ways. Extreme crashes, like the 1987 one-day fall of more than 20%, happen far more often than a bell curve predicts.
